reviews.summary: Against my lens (Cloudflare-primitive correctness within real V2 limits), this PRD is unusually accurate — I verified every load-bearing CF claim against live docs and they hold: Vectorize V2 (10M vectors/index, 50k namespaces/index on Paid, topK 100 without values/metadata dropping to 50 with, 10 metadata indexes, 64B value/namespace caps, 1536 max dims), Workflows (10k default / 25k max steps configurable, 1MiB non-stream step-output cap, ReadableStream bypass), the AI Gateway enforcement boundary (native @cf/ neuron-billed calls are NOT covered by gateway spend limits because they bill via Workers AI pricing not Unified Billing/BYOK — so the app-level token_spend 429 pre-check is the SOLE v1 enforcer, exactly as §5f states), the bge-reranker-base query/contexts[]/top_k/response[] shape + $0.0031/M pricing, bge-m3's documented 60,000-token context + 1024 dims, and the correct framing that a Vectorize namespace is a query-time partition (not a documented security boundary) with the D1 row re-check as the authority. The batch constants (CHUNK=10/EMBED=50/KG=5) and the cf-graph 1MiB-in-memory anti-pattern the PRD fixes both check out against the actual source. What caps the score below 60 is a single CRITICAL but pervasive defect: the iteration-4 product decision to pull entity vector search (brain-entities index + search_entities) INTO v1 was integrated into §1.5/§3.2/§6/§9.2/Appendix but the reconciliation MISSED several runtime-fatal sites — most importantly the self-declared-authoritative §10.1 wrangler manifest, which omits the brain-entities Vectorize BINDING entirely (so ScopedVectorize has no binding to construct → search_entities throws at runtime even though §3.2's create commands make the index exist), and §4.5 line 1409 which AFFIRMATIVELY instructs the KG extraction Workflow to NOT embed/upsert entities in v1 — directly opposing §6.7 flow A which says that same step DOES upsert brain-entities. Two independent runtime-fatal contradictions on the exact decision this re-score was meant to confirm integrated. Plus a medium provisioning contradiction in §7.4 (stale pre-decision metadata-index set including trust_grade, which §3.2 explicitly forbids as an index). The design is feasible and the primitive knowledge is excellent; the integration is incomplete.

strengths: Entity vector search is coherently specified across the DESIGN sections: §3.2 (two-index provisioning + per-index ceilings/metadata budget), §6.1 (entities table now carries embedded_at/embed_error/embedding_model/embedding_dims + entity_fts virtual table), §6.2 (explicit embed-entities Workflow step with retries), §6.3/§6.6 (upsert + scoped search + orphan cleanup against a live index), §6.7 flow A', §6.5 + §9.2.2 tool catalog. Within §6 it is internally consistent end-to-end.

Three of the four product decisions propagated cleanly and consistently: doc/page default visibility='world' (chunks line 601, pages line 640, capability matrix line 1036, decision #2); org=tenant soft-scope row-partitioning with enforced allowed_scopes (§1 Persona C, §7.3, decision #3); and the admin break-glass read, which is unusually thorough — four named gates in §7.6, audit action 'breakglass_read', alert emission, and two dedicated blocking canaries (#14 fail-closed, #15 returns-content-plus-audit-plus-alert).

The facts visibility enum is now the canonical 3-value {private,team,world} in both DDL reproductions (§3.1 line 921 and §8.1 line 3437) and they match, with §3.1 explicitly deferring authority to §8.1.

The section-numbering divergence (inline §N = master-plan numbering, not document headings) is explicitly documented in the convention note and assembly notes, so cross-refs like 'read path is §4.3' / 'backfill spine is §6' are intentional, not errors.
The trust_grade-not-in-Vectorize design is well-argued and self-consistent within §3.2/§5.2 (lives only in the memory_use_policy sidecar, LEFT-JOINed post-hydration).

reviews.summary: Re-score under the completeness/internal-consistency lens, focused on whether entity vector search is now coherent end-to-end and whether the four resolved decisions propagated cleanly. The verdict turns on one unresolved critical: the entity-vector-in-v1 decision is fully specified on the design side (§3.2 provisions brain-entities; §6.2 embed-entities step; §6.3/§6.6 upsert; §6.7 search_entities flow; §9.2.2/§6.5 tool catalog; §6.1 entities table carries embedded_at/embed_error/embedding_model/embedding_dims + entity_fts) but is NOT reconciled at the deploy/binding layer and leaves a trail of stale "deferred to Phase 3.5 / NOT provisioned in v1" markers that directly negate it. Concretely: the §10.1 wrangler.jsonc manifest declares only CHUNKS_INDEX (no ENTITY_INDEX binding) and comments "brain-entities is NOT provisioned in v1"; §10.4 Vectorize provisioning creates only brain-chunks; and §4.4 actively instructs the implementer that "the Workflow does NOT embed entities or upsert to brain-entities in v1." As written, the search_entities / embed-entities code calls a Vectorize binding that does not exist — the feature is internally undeployable. This is a hard contradiction in the requirement set, not mere prose drift, so it caps the score below 60. The fix is mechanical (one binding + index-selection in ScopedVectorize, brain-entities provisioning commands, and ~6 stale-marker edits), and Appendix decision #4 + §3.2 already declare themselves the single source of truth, so the revision direction is unambiguous: update the stale sections to match §3.2, never the reverse. Two secondary inconsistencies in the same deploy layer (trust_grade indexed in §10.4 but explicitly banned as a Vectorize metadata index in §3.2; visibility indexed in §3.2 but omitted in §10.4) compound the picture that §10 was not swept against §3.2. The other three decisions (break-glass, doc default visibility=world, org=tenant row-scoping) are well-propagated and consistent, with only minor residue (break-glass tool missing from the §9.2.2 admin catalog; one stale 2-value facts visibility phrase).

strengths: Break-glass over private memory is fully specified with all four gates: role-gated off the resolved Principal, fails CLOSED for non-admins (403, no private content) incl. the breakGlass:true param path, mandatory in-db.batch memory_audit row carrying actor+target-principal+query (un-bypassable by construction), plus a real-time alert; covered by blocking canaries #14 (fail-closed) and #15 (returns private content AND writes audit AND emits alert).

visibilityPredicate is un-omittable at the single ScopedDB choke-point on EVERY row carrying visibility/team_id/user_id (readFacts, hydrateChunks, and the graph nodeGate), drop-don't-error like the tenant gate; the default recall/think/graph/get_session_context paths provably never bypass it, and owner/admin get no default-path private bypass.

The new brain-entities vector index (search_entities, pulled into v1) carries the identical isolation contract as the chunk arm: namespace=tenantId hard-wired in ScopedVectorize, scope+{world,team}-visibility folded into the metadata filter, then the AUTHORITATIVE D1 re-check on the entities row via scopePredicate + the {world,team} visibilityPredicate; the entity KG node space is consciously {world,team}-only (no private tier) and scope-PARTITIONED in the dedup key, so cross-scope merge is structurally impossible.

Graph arm has no raw-SQL escape hatch: traverse_graph/get_links/get_backlinks/find_orphans/expandFrontier are typed ScopedDB methods that inject tenant_id + scopePredicate (+ visibilityPredicate via nodeGate) on every frontier hop and on seed/anchor resolution (resolveScopedNode/nodeVisible), drop-don't-error with no existence leak; canary #13 tests the entity-arm cross-scope hop.

Cross-scope mint-time escalation fix is correct in the authoritative §7.1/§7.2: a key's allowed_scopes is pinned to intersect(requestedGrant, minter.allowedScopes), so a restricted minter can never widen to '*'; the apiKey.mint audit row records the pinned grant.

Table-driven isolation canary meta-test treats visibility as a third isolation axis spanning facts AND chunks AND the graph/entity arms, so a new read surface that skips readFacts/visibilityPredicate or the typed scope-gated frontier methods fails the meta-test; #1-#15 are required blocking merge checks.

reviews.summary: Re-score under the multi-tenant + intra-tenant isolation lens. The security spine is sound and the four targeted iteration-4/decision items are genuinely landed in the AUTHORITATIVE sections: (1) the admin break-glass read over private memory is role-gated (`requireRole('admin')` off the resolved Principal), fails CLOSED for non-admins incl. `breakGlass:true` without the role (403, returns no private content, §7.6 a/b, canary #14), writes a distinct in-`db.batch` `memory_audit` row with actor + target-principal + query (durable, un-bypassable) and fires a best-effort `waitUntil` alert (canary #15); (2) the default recall/think/graph/get_session_context paths NEVER bypass `visibilityPredicate` — owner/admin do not see others' private/team rows on any default path, break-glass is the single explicit logged carve-out; (3) the new `brain-entities` vector arm (`search_entities`, pulled into v1) carries the SAME gate as chunks — `ScopedVectorize` hard-wires `namespace=tenantId`, scope/{world,team}-visibility folded into the metadata filter, then the authoritative D1 re-check on `entities` via `scopePredicate` + the `{world,team}` `visibilityPredicate` (§3.2/§6.6/§6.7/§9.2.2), and the entity graph arm is scope-partitioned with a typed `nodeGate` (no raw-SQL passthrough); (4) the cross-scope mint-time escalation fix (`allowed_scopes = intersect(requestedGrant, minter.allowedScopes)`) is correct in §7.1/§7.2. No non-admin can reach private content via recall/think/graph/entity-search/break-glass given the AUTHORITATIVE spine. The deductions are reconciliation/threading gaps, not spine breaks: (A) §9.0.1's surface-layer resolver prose is the VERBATIM pre-iter-3 model — the `bk_`/`bdev_` branches state "`allowedScopes` defaults to '*'" and never read the stored `api_keys.allowed_scopes` grant, so an implementer building from §9.0.1 (rather than the §7.2 it points to) reopens the Persona-C CROSS-SCOPE escalation (a client-A staffer's key reading client-B world/team rows; role stays `member` so private stays excluded — NOT a private-content leak); high, not critical, because §9.0.1 explicitly designates §7.2 as authoritative and §7.2 is right. (B) §7.6 mandates an admin-only `memory.break_glass_read` MCP tool and canary #14 calls it, but the §9.2.2 admin catalog omits it. (C) entity-vector-in-v1 (decision #4) is only half-threaded: §3.2/§3.1.4/§6/§9.2.2/appendix say "brain-entities in v1," but §1.3/§1.7/§5.2 still say "deferred to Phase 3.5" and the §7.1 Drizzle `tenant_shards.entityIndex` comment says "deferred, Phase 3.5" and stays nullable — a null `entity_index` would leave `ScopedVectorize` unable to resolve the entity index, breaking `search_entities` operationally (not a leak). No unresolved critical; authoritative isolation spine holds. Low-60s, consistent with the improving 61->62 progression.
